mainTopic: Remarks on illness and healing, then what a person who is מודר הנאה may do with the other person: healing, bathing, sleeping, eating, and working together
overview: The amud opens by finishing a statement that a fever once a month protects the body, and רב נחמן בר יצחק says he would rather have neither the fever nor its benefit. It then explains ערסן, a cooked barley dish that helps the sick. רבי יוחנן says a person with בורדם is not visited and the illness is not named. The גמרא returns to the earlier משנה about a person who is מודר הנאה. It concludes that 'רפואת הנפש' means healing his body, which is allowed, and 'רפואת ממון' means healing his animal, which is forbidden, though advice about the animal is allowed. A new משנה lists shared activities: bathing, sleeping in one bed, reclining, and eating together. A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר forbidding these and רבי יהודה permitting whatever gives no real benefit. A last משנה and גמרא explain that working close to him is forbidden by all, and the argument is only whether to forbid working at a distance as a גזירה.

steps.title: Fever is protective, like thorns around a palm tree
steps.stepSummary: A statement already in progress ends here: a fever once a month protects the body, like thorns protect a palm tree, and works like an antidote.
steps.simpleTranslation: A fever is like thorns for palm trees. If it comes once in thirty days, it is like an antidote for the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that began before this section, saying that a fever can be good for a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thorns guard a palm tree's fruit, and a fever guards the body in the same way. The benefit only holds if the fever is rare, about once in thirty days. Then it works like a cure against harmful things in the body.

keyTerms.meaning: An antidote, a cure against poison

phrases.english: like thorns for palm trees,
phrases.notes: This finishes the earlier line saying a fever is good for the body. Thorns keep people and animals away from the dates.

phrases.english: once in thirty days,
and it is like an antidote for the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a statement about fever begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fever about once a month protects and heals the body.

steps.title: Better to have no fever at all
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says he would rather have neither the fever nor its healing benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: neither it nor its antidote.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the praise of fever. He prefers to skip both the fever and its benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not deny that fever can heal. He just thinks the suffering is not worth the benefit, so he would give up both.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Neither it nor its antidote.
phrases.notes: He means: I would rather not get the fever, even if that means losing the healing it brings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different view in response to the praise of fever.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is better to have no fever, even at the cost of its benefit.

steps.title: ערסן is good for a sick person
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר יונתן, quoting רב יחיאל, says a food called ערסן helps heal the sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר יונתן said in the name of רב יחיאל: ערסן is good for a sick person, to heal him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new health tip: a food called ערסן helps a sick person get better. It does not yet say what ערסן is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new remedy to the earlier talk about illness. Because the word ערסן is not clear, the next steps will have to define it.

keyTerms.meaning: A cooked barley dish given to sick people

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יוֹנָתָן אָמַר רַב יְחִיאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Yonatan said that Rav Yeḥiel said:
Arsan is good for the sick person, for his cure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יוֹנָתָן אָמַר רַב יְחִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement on the same theme of illness and healing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ערסן helps a sick person recover.

steps.title: What is ערסן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word ערסן means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is ערסן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of ערסן. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a plain question to define a word, not a challenge. We cannot use the advice until we know what food it means.

phrases.english: What is arsan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the word used in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What food the word ערסן refers to.

steps.title: First answer: old hulled barley, cooked a long time
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says ערסן is old hulled barley from the first sifting. אביי adds that it must be cooked as long as beef.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said: it is old hulled barley from the beginning of the sifting. אביי said: it needs cooking like the meat of an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן defines ערסן as old hulled barley kernels. אביי adds that it must be cooked for a long time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definition names the grain (barley), its age (old), and which part (the first of the sifting). אביי adds how to prepare it: cook it as long as tough beef.

keyTerms.meaning: Hulled grain, kernels with the husk removed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said:
hulled grains of old barley
from the beginning of the sifting,
Abaye said:
They need cooking like the meat of an ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ערסן is old hulled barley from the first sifting, cooked as long as beef.

steps.title: Second answer: fine flour of old barley
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says ערסן is fine flour ground from old barley from the first sifting. אביי again says it must be cooked like beef.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: it is fine flour of old barley from the beginning of the sifting. אביי said: it needs cooking like the meat of an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a second definition: ground flour, not whole kernels. אביי gives the same cooking note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change from רבי יונתן is the form of the barley: fine flour instead of hulled kernels. Everything else stays the same: old barley, first sifting, long cooking.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
fine flour of old barley
from the beginning of the sifting,
Abaye said:
They need cooking like the meat of an ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 4, different from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ערסן is fine flour of old barley from the first sifting, cooked as long as beef.

steps.title: Do not visit or name the illness בורדם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says we do not visit a person sick with בורדם, and we do not say the name of the illness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: with בורדם, one does not visit the sick person, and one does not mention its name.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives an exception to the usual מצוה of visiting the sick: a person with the illness בורדם is not visited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Visiting the sick is normally a מצוה. This is an exception for one illness, and even its name should not be said. The reason comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
buredam: one does not visit
and one does not mention its name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בּוֹרְדָם אֵין מְבַקְּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement about illness, separate from ערסן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with בורדם is not visited, and the illness is not named.

steps.title: Why not visit him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we would skip visiting this sick person. This sets up רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since visiting the sick is normally good, an exception needs a reason. The question asks for that reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a person with בורדם is not visited.

steps.title: He is like a flowing spring
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the sick person is like a flowing spring, because of constant diarrhea, so a visit would embarrass him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: because he is like a flowing spring.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the reason: this illness makes the body flow nonstop, like a spring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The illness causes constant, uncontrolled discharge. Visitors would cause him shame, so we leave him alone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Because he is like a flowing spring.
phrases.notes: He means the illness causes nonstop diarrhea, so a visit would embarrass him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְּמַעְיָין הַנּוֹבֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sick person is like a flowing spring, so visiting would embarrass him.

steps.title: Why the illness is called בורדם
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר also explains the name בורדם: the sick person is like a flowing spring.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Why is it called בורדם? Because he is like a flowing spring.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds a second teaching: the name of the illness itself points to the same flowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same image, a flowing spring, explains both the rule of not visiting and the name of the illness. The name describes a source that keeps pouring out.

keyTerms.meaning: Why is it called by this name?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Why is it called by the name "buredam"?
phrases.notes: The name can be split into בור (a pit or well) and דם (blood).

phrases.english: Because he is like a flowing spring.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי אלעזר, using the same image to explain the name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name בורדם reflects that the sick person flows like a spring.
steps.whatToRemember: Visiting the sick is normally a מצוה. For בורדם we hold back, because the illness would embarrass the patient.

steps.title: How should we read the משנה's 'healing of the נפש'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about a person who is מודר הנאה. It asks what 'רפואת הנפש' (allowed) versus 'רפואת ממון' (forbidden) means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he heals him with healing of the נפש,' and so on. How is it taught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and asks what its two kinds of healing mean. This sets up a reading that will be rejected and then the correct one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets someone heal a person who is forbidden by vow to benefit from him, but only with 'רפואת הנפש,' not 'רפואת ממון.' The terms are unclear, so the גמרא asks how to understand the line.

keyTerms.meaning: Healing of the 'נפש' (meaning to be clarified)
How is it taught? How should we read it?
A person forbidden by vow to benefit from someone

phrases.english: "And he heals him with healing of the nefesh," etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from our משנה. The 'etc.' stands for the rest: 'but not healing of ממון.'

phrases.english: How is it taught?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topics on illness and returns to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'רפואת הנפש' and 'רפואת ממון' mean in the משנה.

steps.title: It cannot mean free versus paid
steps.stepSummary: If the terms meant healing for free versus for a fee, the משנה should have just said 'for free, but not for a fee.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say healing of the נפש means for free and healing of ממון means for pay, then let it teach this: he heals him for free, but not for pay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible reading, free versus paid, and knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is about wording. If the משנה meant free versus paid, it would use those plain words. Since it chose 'נפש' and 'ממון,' those terms must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach it this way

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'רפואת ממון' as 'healing done for money.' The גמרא rejects that reading here.

phrases.english: If you say that healing of the nefesh means for free,
and healing of mamon means for pay,
let it teach this:
He heals him for free, but not for pay!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a reading of the question in step 11 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that נפש/ממון means free/paid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the meaning, the משנה would have said 'free' and 'for pay' plainly.

steps.title: נפש means his body, ממון means his animal
steps.stepSummary: The correct reading: 'רפואת הנפש' is healing the person's body (allowed), and 'רפואת ממון' is healing his animal (forbidden).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: healing of the נפש is his body, and healing of ממון is his animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning. You may heal the person himself, but not his animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The terms describe what is being healed, not how much it costs. Healing a person's body is allowed even though he is מודר הנאה. Healing his animal, which is his property, is forbidden benefit.

phrases.english: Rather: healing of the nefesh is his body,
healing of mamon is his animal.
phrases.notes: His animal is called ממון because it is part of his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of step 12 with the correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נפש = the person's body (allowed to heal); ממון = his animal (forbidden to heal).

steps.title: He may still give advice about the animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי זוטרא בר טוביה in the name of רב: he may not treat the animal, but he may say which medicine is good or bad for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: But he may say to him, 'Such-and-such medicine is good for it, such-and-such medicine is bad for it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds an exception to the ban on healing the animal: the healer may still give advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Treating the animal is forbidden benefit. Telling the owner which medicine helps or harms is only advice, and that is allowed. So the ban covers the act of healing, not sharing knowledge.

keyTerms.meaning: But he may say to him

steps.whatToRemember: With a person who is מודר הנאה: you may heal his body. You may not heal his animal. You may still advise him about which medicines help or harm the animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: It draws a practical line between doing something for a person, which is forbidden benefit, and only telling him useful information, which is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zutra bar Toviya said that Rav said:
But he may say to him:
"Such-and-such medicine is good for it,
such-and-such medicine is bad for it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב אֲבָל אוֹמֵר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule in step 13 that one may not heal the animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He may not treat the animal, but he may advise which medicine is good or bad for it.

steps.title: Bathing and sleeping together
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows bathing together in a large bath but not a small one, and allows sharing a bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He may bathe with him in a large bath, but not in a small one. And he may sleep with him in a bed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and lists things a person may do together with someone who is forbidden to benefit from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a large bath, one body does not change the water, so no benefit passes between them. In a small bath, one person's body changes the water's temperature, and that counts as giving benefit. So bathing in a small bath together is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A bath or tub of water

phrases.english: MISHNA: And he may bathe with him in a large bath,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the person who is not allowed to get any benefit from the other one.

phrases.english: but not in a small one.
And he may sleep with him in a bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה that continues the list of what is allowed to someone who is מודר הנאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bathing together in a large bath is allowed. In a small bath it is forbidden. Sharing a bed is allowed.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits sharing a bed to summer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says sharing a bed is only allowed in summer, because in winter one person's body warms the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: in the summer, but not in the rainy season, because he gives him benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a limit to the rule about sharing a bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In winter, body heat warms the bed, so the other person benefits. In summer, extra warmth does not help anyone. The test is the same as with the bath: does real benefit pass from one person to the other?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: in the days of summer,
but not in the rainy season,
because he gives him benefit.
phrases.notes: The benefit is warmth. In a cold season, his body heat warms the bed for the other person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the first opinion's permission to share a bed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sharing a bed is allowed only in summer. In winter it is forbidden because of the warmth one gives the other.

steps.title: Reclining and eating at the same table
steps.stepSummary: He may recline and eat with him, but not from one shared platter, unless it is a platter that goes back to the host.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he may recline with him on a couch. And he may eat with him at the table, but not from the platter. But he may eat with him from the platter that returns.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with reclining together and eating together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reclining on one couch gives no benefit, so it is allowed in every season. Eating from one shared platter is a problem, because food one person leaves becomes extra food for the other. A platter that 'returns' has enough for everyone, so no one gets more because of the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Reclines, as people did at a meal

steps.confusionAlert: Eating at the same table is fine. The only problem is eating from the same platter, unless it is the 'returning' kind.

phrases.english: And he may recline with him on a couch.
And he may eat with him at the table,
but not from the platter.
But he may eat with him
from the platter that returns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list with eating-related cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reclining and eating at one table are allowed. Eating from one shared platter is forbidden, except from a 'returning' platter.

steps.title: רבי מאיר forbids bathing and sleeping together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that, according to רבי מאיר, bathing and sleeping together are forbidden whether the bath or bed is large or small.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught in a ברייתא: He may not bathe with him in a bath, and he may not sleep with him in a bed, whether large or small. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows who holds the strictest view: רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה permitted a large bath and sharing a bed. The ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר forbids both, no matter the size. He sets this up as the opposite side to רבי יהודה, who comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: These are the words of רבי מאיר

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ תַּנְיָא: לֹא יִרְחַץ עִמּוֹ בְּאַמְבָּטִי,
phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught: He may not bathe with him in a bath,
and he may not sleep with him in a bed,
whether large or small,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that lays out the full argument behind the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר forbids bathing and sleeping together, whatever the size.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's fuller view in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה allows a large bed in winter and a small bed in summer. He allows bathing in a large bath and sweating in a small one. He also allows reclining and eating at one table, but not from a shared platter unless it is a returning one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a large bed in the rainy season and a small bed in summer is permitted. He may bathe with him in a large bath and sweat with him in a small one. But he may recline with him on a couch and eat with him at the table, but not from the platter. But he may eat from the platter that returns.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יהודה's side, which is more lenient than רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the only question is whether real benefit passes. A large bed in winter leaves enough space that body heat does not help the other person. In summer warmth does not help at all, so even a small bed is fine. Sweating together in a small bath, as opposed to bathing in its water, also gives no benefit.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'large' and 'small' at the start refer to the bed, not the bath. The bath comes up only in the next line.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: גְּדוֹלָה בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: a large one in the rainy season,
phrases.notes: He is talking about the bed here.

phrases.english: and a small one in the summer, is permitted.
He may bathe with him in a large bath,
and sweat with him in a small one.
But he may recline with him on a couch
and eat with him at the table,
but not from the platter.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אוֹכֵל הוּא מִן הַתַּמְחוּי הַחוֹזֵר.
phrases.english: But he may eat from the platter that returns.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: גְּדוֹלָה בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The other side of the argument in the same ברייתא, against רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wherever no benefit passes between them, the activity is allowed: a large bed in winter, a small bed in summer, a large bath, sweating in a small bath, reclining, eating at one table, and eating from a returning platter.

steps.title: What a 'returning platter' means
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains that the 'returning platter' is one that goes back to the host.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: from the platter that returns to the host.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains the unclear phrase 'the platter that returns.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If leftovers go back to the host, the guests are not eating up each other's share. Each person eats from the host's food. That is why eating together from such a platter gives no benefit from one diner to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: The host, the owner of the house

steps.whatToRemember: The rule for this whole section: an activity done together is allowed only if one person does not end up benefiting from the other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
from the platter that returns to the host.
phrases.notes: There is plenty of food, and the leftovers go back to the host. So neither guest is eating the other's portion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: מִן הַתַּמְחוּי הַחוֹזֵר לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a term used in both the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The permitted 'returning platter' is one whose leftovers go back to the host.

steps.title: Eating and working near hired laborers
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: רבי מאיר forbids eating with him from the laborers' food bowl and working beside him in the same row. חכמים allow working if he stays at a distance.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: He may not eat with him from the large bowl in front of the laborers, and he may not work with him in the same row. These are the words of רבי מאיר. And the חכמים say: he may work, as long as he is far from him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about workers who eat and work side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating from the workers' shared bowl could leave the other person extra food. Working in the same row helps the other person, since each one's work makes the other's job easier. חכמים say that working at a distance avoids this, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A large bowl of food set out for workers
A row of vines or plants worked together

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא יֹאכַל עִמּוֹ מִן הָאֵבוּס
phrases.english: MISHNA: He may not eat with him from the large bowl
that is in front of the laborers,
and he may not work with him in the same row,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עוֹשֶׂה וְהוּא בָּרָחוֹק מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: he may work, as long as he is far from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא יֹאכַל עִמּוֹ מִן הָאֵבוּס שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַפּוֹעֲלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה with more cases of shared activity, now in a work setting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר forbids eating from the workers' bowl and working in the same row. חכמים allow working in the row if he keeps his distance.

steps.title: Both sides agree that working close by is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that when the two work close together, everyone agrees it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: When they work close to each other, nobody argues. It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by marking off the case where there is no argument at all. This sets up the next step, which shows where the real argument is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only showed the חכמים allowing work 'at a distance,' so we might wonder what each side holds about working close by. The גמרא says plainly that close work is forbidden according to everyone. That narrows the argument to the distant case alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
In a close case, they do not disagree that it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: 'Close' means working right next to him in the same row, the case from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's explanation of the משנה in step 21 by defining the case where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Working close beside the other person is forbidden according to both רבי מאיר and the חכמים.

steps.title: The argument is only about working at a distance
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר forbids working at a distance as a protective rule because of working close by, where loosening the soil helps the other person. The רבנן do not make that protective rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they do argue is when they work far apart. רבי מאיר holds that we forbid working far apart because of working close by, since close by he loosens the earth in front of the other person. The רבנן hold that we do not make that protective rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the exact point of the argument, which is working at a distance. It also gives the reason behind each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Working close by is forbidden because his digging loosens the soil in front of the other person, which is a real benefit to him. רבי מאיר adds a גזירה: forbid even distant work so people won't come to work close by. The רבנן don't add this extra fence, so for them distant work is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: We make a protective rule (גְּזֵרָה) to keep people away from the real prohibition
The Sages, here the same as the חכמים of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Close work: forbidden by all, because loosening the soil helps the other person. Distant work: רבי מאיר forbids it as a גזירה, and the רבנן allow it.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר does not think distant work itself gives any benefit. He forbids it only as a fence, so people won't end up working close by.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is when they are at a distance.
Rabbi Meir holds:
We forbid distant work as a protective rule because of close work,
since he loosens the earth in front of him.
And the Rabbis hold: we do not make that protective rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 22's point of agreement by locating the argument in the distant case and explaining each side's reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר forbids distant work as a גזירה because of close work, which gives the other person benefit by loosening the soil. The רבנן do not make this גזירה and allow distant work.
